Job Description

At Netcompany, we are looking for both newly graduated candidates with a relevant master’s degree – or equivalent experience – who want to work as IT Consultants at the intersection of technology, business, and people. Do you want to help develop some of Denmark’s most complex and business-critical IT solutions, where software development, project management, and close client collaboration are central parts of everyday work?

Responsibilities and technologies

As an IT Consultant, you help translate client needs into the right technical solution. We choose the technologies that best fit each project and client. As a result, you should enjoy working across a variety of technologies and domains, while continuously expanding your knowledge and expertise.

A large part of our projects is based on web technologies such as Angular or React, and Java or C# on either a Java or .NET platform. In addition, we work with a wide range of standard platforms including Microsoft, Salesforce, IBM, Oracle, Adobe, Snowflake, Guidewire, and others.

As an IT Consultant, you contribute to all parts of system development with a focus on technical tasks. Your responsibilities will vary from project to project and evolve over time, but your responsibilites will typically include:

• Setting up and developing frameworks and integrations.

• Implementing features in user interfaces.

• Configuring and developing extensions for standard platforms.

• Automating business processes, for example through batch jobs.

• Developing tools and scripts for migrating large volumes of data.

You will join a team with colleagues from diverse backgrounds and areas of expertise. What we all have in common is a technical mindset and shared ambition to build the best possible IT solutions together.

Our projects include some of Denmark’s most innovative and mission-critical IT initiatives across the public and private sectors, meaning you will help shape and improve everyday life for a large part of society.

About you

We expect you to hold a masters's degree in engineering, computer science, software, IT, or a similar field. To succeed in this role, you:

• Are a recent graduate or have a couple of years of experience – most importantly, you are passionate about taking your IT career to the next level.

• Possess strong technical skills in object-oriented programming.

• Have a solid understanding of software development and motivated to further develop your skills.

• Think analytically, show initiative, and work in a structured way.

• Full professional proficiency in Swedish and English (written and spoken) is a must. As you will be working closely with Danish clients and colleagues, you should be able to communicate and collaborate effectively in a Danish work environment.

Continue developing with us

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars on everything from technologies to customer management. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills, preparing you for various tasks and continuously improving your expertise throughout your career with us.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

Send us your application

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance. #LI-SA1

Company Description

Are you motivated by helping people and business functions unlock the value of AI in their daily work? Do you thrive in a role where you influence, enable, and drive change across a large international organisation?

As our new AI Business Enablement Lead, you will play a key role in accelerating AI adoption across JYSK. Based at our Head Office in Aarhus, you will work closely with business leaders and colleagues across functions to turn AI opportunities into practical solutions that create value.

This is a unique opportunity to join a newly established AI function and shape how AI becomes part of the way we work. As the first person in this role, you will help build the foundation for future growth while working closely with the Central AI team and stakeholders across the business.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

At JYSK, we believe that dedication creates opportunities. We offer you a role with a high degree of responsibility, visibility, and influence across the organisation. You will join a company where decisions are made quickly, ideas are welcomed, and colleagues work together with trust, respect, and a shared ambition to improve how we do business.

You will become part of a growing AI function that supports colleagues across JYSK, helping business areas build confidence and capability in using AI. At the same time, you will have excellent opportunities for both professional and personal development in an international environment.

As our first recruit in this new AI function, you will set the benchmark. For the right candidate with a strong, proactive mindset, this role offers a clear path to grow into leading our future team of AI Business Enablement Specialists.

Furthermore, we offer you:

• A unique opportunity to shape and drive AI adoption across JYSK

• Significant exposure to senior stakeholders and business leaders across functions

• Close collaboration with AI specialists, engineers, and data professionals

• A workplace built on trust, empowerment, and freedom with responsibility

• A modern Head Office environment in Aarhus with a strong team culture

• Attractive employee benefits, social activities, and staff discounts

• Opportunities for continuous learning, development, and future career growth

WHAT YOUR NEXT JOB WILL BE ABOUT

You will act as a trusted partner to business functions, supporting leaders and teams in identifying, prioritising, and implementing AI opportunities. Through training, coaching, stakeholder engagement, and structured change management, you will help ensure that AI becomes a natural and valuable part of daily work across JYSK.

Your success will depend on your ability to build relationships, simplify complex topics, and guide colleagues through transformation in a practical and business-focused way.

Your tasks and responsibilities in the job include:

• Partnering with business leaders to identify, evaluate, and prioritise high-value AI use cases

• Designing and delivering practical AI training, workshops, and enablement activities for business users

• Establishing best practices, reusable frameworks, prompt libraries, responsible AI practices and AI adoption guidelines

• Driving AI adoption strategies and supporting departments on their AI maturity journey

• Collaborating closely with the Central AI team to evaluate initiatives and determine the right solution approach

• Monitoring business impact, and value creation through defined success metrics

• Engage with the broader AI Ambassador network to improve usage and adoption of AI across all units at JYSK.

• Facilitating cross-functional collaboration to reduce duplication and promote shared learning across JYSK

WHAT SHOULD YOU BRING

We are looking for someone who combines strong business understanding with the ability to drive change and inspire others. You are comfortable working across functions, navigating ambiguity, and helping colleagues understand how AI can support their goals.

You bring a practical and collaborative approach, and you enjoy turning new technologies into meaningful business outcomes.

We are looking for a new colleague who:

• Has 5-7 years of relevant experience

• Holds a degree in Business, Information Systems, Innovation Management, Engineering, or a related field

• Has proven experience driving change management, transformation, or business improvement initiatives across an organisation

• Demonstrates strong practical experience with AI tools, enterprise copilots, prompt engineering, and AI-enabled workflows

• Has excellent stakeholder management skills and can influence without direct authority

• Can assess, prioritise, and communicate business value from AI use cases

• Enjoys coaching and enabling colleagues while creating engagement around new ways of working

Additional Information

IS THIS YOUR NEXT OPPORTUNITY? Apply today!

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Head of AI, Karan Honavar at +45 2812 8374.

We kindly ask you to only attach your CV. With us, there is no need to write a traditional cover letter when applying for a job.

Instead, when you click “I’m interested/Apply”, you will have the option to write a brief message to the hiring team. If you wish, you can use this space to share your motivation for applying or highlight anything else you feel is relevant.

ABOUT US

We believe our employees are key to our success. That is why we strive to offer development and possibilities of growing and finding new challenges within JYSK. Since our founder, Lars Larsen, opened his first store in Denmark in 1979, JYSK has expanded our global presence with stores and web shops in countries around the world.

Our three fundamental JYSK Values – Tradesman, Colleague and Corporate Spirit – express the behaviour and attitude that we can expect from each other. We trust each other, and we believe in Empowerment and freedom with responsibility. We also take pride in rewarding engagement and a great effort among our employees. With the right attitude, opportunities abound in JYSK.

JYSK wants to include everyone, no matter the age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, and experience. Together, we secure our inclusive culture that encourages, supports, and celebrates the diverse voices of our employees. Because a great mix of minds, talents and unique personalities makes us a stronger team.

Would you like to turn structure, analysis and practical coordination into more effective crisis readiness? Join TDC NET and help maintain and develop the framework, tools and training that support our Crisis Management Team.

TDC NET owns and operates digital infrastructure that is critical to Denmark. Our Crisis Management framework helps the organisation respond when serious events require fast coordination, clear decisions and reliable communication. You will join the Business Continuity and Crisis Management area and work closely with experienced colleagues and stakeholders across the organisation.

About the job

We are looking for a motivated and structured student assistant who wants to learn how crisis readiness is built in practice. You will support both the day-to-day maintenance of our Crisis Management framework and the continued development of the Crisis Management Team. The role combines practical coordination, document and data management, analysis, communication and continuous improvement work.

You will receive clear priorities and guidance, but you will also be trusted to be responsible for defined tasks and follow them through. Your work will contribute directly to making plans easier to use, training more effective, and improvement actions more visible.

Purpose of the role

Your purpose is to help keep our crisis-management setup current, organised and ready for use. You will support documents, exercises, readiness activities, reporting and follow-up, while learning how operational resilience and executive crisis management work in a large infrastructure company.

Key responsibilities

• Maintain and improve crisis plans, appendices, role descriptions, quick guides, checklists and templates.

• Coordinate practical preparation for workshops, activation drills and crisis exercises, including invitations, rooms, Teams setup, materials and participant data.

• Collect and structure data from training, activations and exercises, and prepare clear overviews and PowerPoint material.

• Maintain action and improvement trackers, follow up with owners and prepare concise status updates.

• Support stronger decision logging, situation reporting, briefing flows and role-ready crisis-room materials.

• Carry out desk research on crisis management, operational resilience, emerging risks and best practice.

• Help explore, test and responsibly apply AI to improve crisis preparedness, response, recovery, decision and action logging, situation reporting and post-incident learning.

What you will work on from the start

Recent exercises have identified practical opportunities to make activation faster, clarify interfaces, improve decision and situation reporting. We also want to explore how responsible use of AI can improve crisis preparedness, response, recovery, reporting and continuous learning. You will help turn these lessons into updated tools, training material, trackers and follow-up activities. You will support the work, while decisions and formal ownership remain with the relevant specialists and leaders.

Your first months

During your first months, you will learn the Crisis Management framework, key roles, exercise cycle and improvement backlog. With support from the team, you will gradually take ownership of recurring practical tasks, selected improvement actions and clearly defined deliverables. You will be expected to keep overviews current, flag issues early, and ask for guidance when decisions or sensitive information are involved.

The role is designed to combine learning with real responsibility. You will work close to both operational specialists and senior stakeholders, but you will not make crisis decisions or replace specialist role holders. Your contribution is to make the process, tools, information and follow-up more reliable and easier to use.

“You will not just help maintain documents. You will help us turn lessons from exercises into practical improvements that enhance how the organisation prepares, coordinates and responds to a crisis.”

- Noah Fröhlich, Head of Business Continuity, TDC NET

About you

We imagine that you:

• Are enrolled in a relevant higher-education programme, for example emergency and risk management, security, political science, business, engineering, communication, law or a similar field.

• Work in a structured way, pay attention to detail and reliably finish what you start.

• Can turn complex information into clear notes, simple overviews and well-structured slides.

• Are curious, proactive and comfortable asking questions when something is unclear.

• Are skilled using Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel and Word, or motivated to become so quickly.

• Have AI fluency, practical experience with AI tools or a genuine interest in learning how AI can be used responsibly in crisis management.

• Communicate fluently in English, both in writing and verbally.

• Can handle sensitive information responsibly and exercise sound judgement.

• Are able to obtain and maintain the security clearance required for the position. Employment will be conditional on successful security approval.

• Can work approximately 15–20 hours per week, with flexibility around exam periods.

Previous experience with crisis management is not required. We value your structure, judgement, curiosity and willingness to learn.

What you will gain

• Practical experience with crisis management, business continuity and operational resilience in critical infrastructure.

• Insight into how executive teams prepare for and manage serious incidents.

• Experience planning exercises, analysing results and converting lessons into practical improvements.

• Enhanced capabilities in structured problem solving, project coordination, data analysis and executive communication.

• Close collaboration with experienced colleagues across technology, security, operations, communications, legal and senior management.

• The opportunity to take real responsibility for defined deliverables and see the impact of your work.

Contact:

As a Solution Engineer – Privileged Access Management (PAM) & Identity Infrastructure at TDC NET, you will play a key role in designing, implementing, and operating enterprise Identity and Privileged Access Management solutions. You will be responsible for securing privileged access across infrastructure, applications, cloud platforms, and operational technology while ensuring seamless integration with Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, PKI, and modern automation practices.

About the job

Working closely with Infrastructure, Security, Platform Engineering, and Application teams, you will help automate identity services, improve security controls, and improve operational efficiency through Infrastructure-as-Code and modern engineering practices.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Design, implement, configure, and maintain enterprise PAM solutions.

• Integrate servers, applications, databases, network devices, and cloud platforms into the PAM ecosystem.

• Manage and support Microsoft Active Directory, Entra ID , LDAP, MFA and related identity services.

• Support and maintain Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), including certificate lifecycle management and secure authentication mechanisms.

• Automate PAM and identity-related processes using Infrastructure-as-Code and scripting.

• Monitor platform performance, troubleshoot complex technical issues, and continuously improve platform stability and security.

• Identify security risks and implement mitigation strategies aligned with enterprise security standards.

• Provide technical guidance and knowledge sharing across engineering teams.

"We are building more than an IAM platform. We are building a modern identity engineering capability. If you enjoy solving complex security challenges, driving automation, and making a real impact, you'll fit right in with our team."

– Abhishek Kumar, Senior Manager – Identity & Access Management, TDC NET

About you

You are passionate about Identity & Access Management, infrastructure security, and automation. You enjoy solving complex technical challenges and continuously improving enterprise security platforms through modern engineering practices.

You thrive in collaborative environments where Security, Infrastructure, Cloud, and DevOps come together to build secure and scalable identity services.

Required Qualifications

• 4+ years of experience working with Identity & Access Management (IAM), Privileged Access Management (PAM), or Security Infrastructure.

• Extensive experience with Microsoft Active Directory, Entra ID, Group Policy, LDAP, and key authentication technologies.

• Solid understanding & experience with Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), certificate lifecycle management, TLS/SSL, and authentication mechanisms

• Experience with Keycloak, Hashicorp vault , Ping or equivalent platforms

• Practical experience implementing, configuring, and supporting Delinea Privileged Access Management (PAM), HashiCorp Boundary, or equivalent privileged access solutions.

• Solid understanding of authentication and authorization protocols such as Kerberos, LDAP, SAML, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), and RADIUS.

• Experience operating in highly regulated enterprise settings, with a solid graspof security frameworks, compliance requirements, and audit controls.

• Extensive troubleshooting skills across Windows, Linux, and enterprise infrastructure.

• Advanced analytical, problem-solving, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to communicate complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Applicants are required to meet the criteria for submitting a security clearance application.

Good to Have

• Experience working with HashiCorp Vault for secrets management and privileged credential management.

• Experience using Terraform for Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and automation.

• Experience using Git and modern version control workflows.

• Experience with CI/CD platforms such as Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, or similar DevOps pipelines.

• Experience with PowerShell, Bash, or Python scripting for automation and operational tasks.

• Familiarity with container platforms such as Docker or Kubernetes.

What We Offer

At TDC NET, you'll join a collaborative engineering team focused on building and operating modern Identity and Privileged Access Management services that protect critical infrastructure and enable secure digital transformation.

You'll have the opportunity to work with modern IAM technologies, automation, Infrastructure-as-Code, and cloud identity services while influencing technical direction and helping shape the future of our identity engineering capabilities.

If solving challenging security issues and improving identity, automation, and privileged access sounds appealing, we'd be happy to hear from you.

WHOLESALE ACCOUNT EXECUTIVE FOR DENMARK AT BY MALENE BIRGER

By Malene Birger is currently looking for a Wholesale Account Executive for

the Danish market.

Key responsibilities

As Wholesale Account Executive for the DK region (Denmark incl. Faroe Island, Greenland and Iceland) you will be

essential at accelerating the brand’s growth within your designated territories. Reporting directly to the Danish

headquarters and the Commercial Director based in Copenhagen, you will develop strategic initiatives, nurture key

partnerships, and act as a passionate brand ambassador. We expect you to be based out of Denmark, conscious

that regular travel in your designated markets will be essential to foster relationships, monitor market dynamics,

and showcase collections in your market. Travel should be expected 3/5 days a week, with majority of the travel

executed across the Danish region, with 1-2 visits per year in the areas outside of Denmark.

It is required that the candidate holds a valid driver’s license.

This is a dynamic and rewarding role, requiring a flexible and agile lifestyle, operational abilities, and exceptional

relationship management, perfect for a mid-level candidate ready to take on further responsibilities.

Market Development & Sales Planning

• Execute tailored sales strategies, business plans, and market entry initiatives aligned with brand

positioning and long-term growth objectives aligned with Danish HQ growth strategies.

• Conduct ongoing competitive analysis, market research, and consumer insight gathering to identify

emerging trends, customer needs, and competitive opportunities.

• Assistant Management to forecast sales, pipelines, and budgets to ensure sustained revenue growth,

market share expansion, and achievement of key performance indicators.

Relationship Management & Business Development

• Cultivate and sustain high-value relationships with existing accounts and partners through regular on-site

visits, to nurture and secure ongoing engagement from Partners and their sales force.

• Identify and pursue new business opportunities, frequent visit of prospects, and strategic partnerships

aligned with brand objectives.

• Lead onboarding of new accounts and develop go-to-market strategies, ensuring seamless integration and

ongoing development.

Partnership Excellence & Brand Representation

• Maintain high standards of service and partnership, including visual merchandising support, reorder

services and product training, positioning By Malene Birger as a preferred and strategic collaborator within

your markets.

• Represent the brand actively at international trade shows, fashion weeks, and industry events, embodying

and communicating the brand’s values and aesthetic.

• Develop and deliver tailored sales presentations and collection showcases (4 times annually) in key

Copenhagen and Paris.

• Coordinate and operate the Copenhagen showroom for selling in periods, including but not limited to;

sales planning, sales execution, samples coordination, VM and logistics showroom room planning.

Operational Collaboration & Cross-Functional Alignment

• Work closely with marketing, product development, logistics, and finance teams to ensure alignment of

commercial, branding, and operational objectives and company policies.

• Provide detailed, proactive market feedback to influence collection planning, messaging strategies, and

marketing initiatives to maintain relevance and drive desirability.

• Oversee the management and advancement of the sales pipeline and forecasting tools, ensuring accurate

tracking of performance and future planning.

Product Training & Service Excellence

• Support and guide sales teams and partners through product training and brand education to maximize

sales impact.

• Ensure consistent, high-quality customer experience in all wholesale interactions, fostering loyalty and

brand advocacy across any touch point with the brand.

Skillset and attributes

Professional

• 2-3 years of experience within wholesale, B2B sales, and/or account management within the fashion,

interior or luxury industry.

• Successful experience with executing sales strategies, managing sales budgets, and reaching targets.

• Good understanding of market dynamics, industry trends, and consumer insights to inform strategic

decisions.

• Fluency in Danish and English is mandatory, further language within the designated area is considered a

plus.

• Flair for analytical, preferably with proficiency in sales reporting tools, CRM platforms, and Microsoft

Office, especially Excel.

• Driver’s license is a requirement to possess the role.

Personal

• Outgoing, and relationship-centric personality, with authentic interpersonal and communication skills.

• Performance driven, curious, organized, and capable of working both independently and as part of a

dedicated team across different cultures and environments.

• High level of agility and resilience to navigate a fast-paced, dynamic market landscape.

• Great emotional intelligence, active listening skills, and an empathetic approach to client and partner

relationships.

Help shape how AI is used at MyDefence from strategy and architecture to working solutions.

AI is moving fast. For us, the ambition is not to adopt technology simply because it is new, but to understand where it can create real value and build the right foundations to use it responsibly.

We are looking for an AI Implementation Lead who can help shape and implement MyDefence’s approach to artificial intelligence. This is a role for someone who enjoys working at the intersection of strategy and hands-on technology: someone who can think about architecture, governance and long-term direction – and then turn ideas into proof-of-concepts that demonstrate what is actually possible.

You will join our IT & Security organisation, report to our CISO and become a go-to person for AI across MyDefence, working with teams across the whole global organisation.

What you will do

Your role will span AI strategy, architecture, governance and hands-on implementation. You will help us identify where AI can make a meaningful difference as well as where it should not be applied.

A key part of your role will be turning direction into something tangible. You will build and demonstrate proof-of-concepts, work with technologies such as Microsoft Azure AI Foundry, agentic frameworks and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and help move successful concepts towards production.

Your key responsibilities will include:

AI strategy, architecture & governance

• Design MyDefence’s AI strategy, together with a Global AI-team, and target architecture, and turn it into concrete, deliverable initiatives.

• Provide governance and oversight of AI adoption, ensuring it is responsible, compliant, and aligned with company priorities.

• Assess opportunities and risks and recommend where AI should and should not be applied.

Technical delivery & proof-of-concept

• Build and demonstrate proof-of-concepts hands-on using tools such as Microsoft Azure AI Foundry, AWS Bedrock, and similar platforms.

• Translate strategy into working implementations and guide their move from concept to production.

Data foundations

• Ensure the data foundations for AI are sound - proper data quality, structures, and governance are prerequisites for reliable AI.

• Work with consultants and internal teams to get data structures right so AI can be implemented and deliver value on top of them.

• Apply business data analytics skills to connect data, AI, and real business needs.

Staying at the frontier

• Track developments across the AI field, including what leading providers such as

• Anthropic and OpenAI are shipping and current best practices.

• Maintain a clear-eyed view of pitfalls and risks so MyDefence adopts the right technologies and avoids the wrong ones.

Who we are looking for

You are curious about where AI is going and focused on turning new technology into real value. You combine technical expertise with a pragmatic, hands-on approach.

You have a relevant degree in computer science, data science, engineering or a similar field or equivalent professional experience, along with experience designing and implementing AI solutions.

We imagine that you bring:

• Proven experience designing and implementing AI solutions, including hands-on proof-of-concept work.

• Hands-on experience with modern AI platforms such as Microsoft Azure AI Foundry, AWS Bedrock, Copilot-studio.

• Experience working with agentic frameworks and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems.

• A solid understanding of data structures, data quality, and business data analytics.

• The ability to communicate AI concepts, opportunities and risks clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Professional proficiency in English, both written and spoken.

• Experience with responsible AI adoption and relevant compliance considerations is considered an advantage.

Who you are

You are curious by nature and genuinely interested in where AI is heading, but you also have a critical eye and know how to separate hype from solutions that create real value. You enjoy working in a fast-moving field and are motivated by both exploring new possibilities and turning them into something tangible.

We see you as someone who:

• Is curious and continuously learning, keeping up with developments and best practices within AI.

• Takes a pragmatic and delivery-focused approach, balancing strategic thinking with getting things built.

• Thinks critically about opportunities, risks, and limitations rather than adopting technology for technology’s sake.

• Communicates complex topics clearly and enjoys working with both technical and non-technical colleagues.

• Works well across teams and is comfortable collaborating with consultants, vendors and partners.

• Is comfortable working in a security-conscious environment where confidentiality and responsible decision-making are essential.

What we stand for

At MyDefence, we live by a shared set of values that guide us – both in how we do business and in our everyday interactions as colleagues. These values are our compass, ensuring that we move toward the same goal with courage, execution, and care.

We Dare (Courage)

We challenge the status quo, embrace new ideas, and have the courage to make decisions that move us forward.

We Do (Execution)

We take ownership, deliver on our commitments, and turn ideas into action.

We Care (I Am Your Wing(wo)man)

We support one another, succeed as a team, and build strong relationships based on trust and respect.

How to apply

If you're motivated by building, improving, and challenging the status quo rather than simply maintaining what's already in place, we'd love to hear from you.

Questions? If you have any questions about the role, please do not hesitate to reach out to Casper Skyum Høgh, who will be happy to provide further details about the position.

Submit your application and CV as soon as possible; we review applications on a rolling basis and may close the position once we have found the right candidate.

jobs.description:
We are looking for one or two highly motivated research assistants for 4-month period to investigate how a long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) variant of ASCC3 regulates transcriptional recovery following DNA damage, in the Svejstrup lab, DNRF Center of Excellence, Center for Gene Expression (CGEN), Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine (ICMM), Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. Staring date: January 1, 2027

  Previous work from the Svejstrup group identified two gene products of ASCC3 implicated in this response: a protein, encoded by the long mRNA transcript, that suppresses transcription during the late stages of the UV-induced global shutdown; and a short mRNA transcript that acts as a regulatory lncRNA, suppressing the ASCC3 protein's function and enabling transcriptional recovery.

  The project will be focused on understanding how the ASCC3 lncRNA regulates RNAPII-mediated transcription and its recovery after DNA damage, using CRISPR/Cas9 technologies to generate and manipulate ASCC3 transcript variants, combined with state-of-the-art transcription profiling approaches such as TTchem-seq and RNA-seq.

  Information on the Department can be found at: https://icmm.ku.dk/english/ 

   

  Our Center and Research
 CGEN is an interdisciplinary research center consisting of 6 research groups located in modern laboratories in the Mærsk Tower at the Panum Institute. Our mission is to use a cutting-edge ensemble of genetic, cell biological, biochemical, organismal, and modern ‘omic’-approaches to achieve a comprehensive understanding of the process of gene expression.

  CGEN performs ground-breaking research in a collaborative and ambitious environment, where young researchers are offered the best conditions to engage in bold and imaginative research. CGEN is also a center of learning, where PhDs and postdocs receive comprehensive insights in the cellular processes underlying gene expression, as well as a clear view of their medical importance and potential for a future research carreer.

jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Copenhagen (UCPH), invites applications for a fully funded 3-year PhD-position from 1 May 2027 or after agreement.  
 
 The position and the project
 The successful candidate will work on the project Treatments for Complex PTSD (RECONNECT-trial), a randomized controlled trial conducted in the Mental Health Services. The project has a strong focus on patient involvement and investigating mechanisms of change within the three intervention arms (Prolonged Exposure, Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing and Enhanced Emotional and Interpersonal Skills Training). The project is conducted in collaboration between researchers in psychology and psychiatry.
 
 Duties and responsibilities
 The PhD student will be central in the research project, being involved in and responsible for large parts of the data collection. Most importantly, the PhD-student will be responsible for conceptualizing and conducting a subset of studies. As such, data management and data analyses, as well as manuscript preparation and communication of research results to the scientific community as well as to relevant stakeholders will be central.

  The PhD-student will be responsible for the assessment of the participants with the International Trauma Interview in Danish, overseeing recruitment progress, and conducting quantitative and qualitative research based on survey and interview data. Experience with quantitative and qualitative data analysis is a must. The candidate must have strong clinical skills and preferably with trauma populations. The candidate must be able to work independently under supervision. Collaborative skills and team spirit are in high regard. For the right candidate, there will be ample possibilities to influence the project and develop new project ideas within the project frame.
 
 Supervision and research group
 The PhD-student will be part of a research group at the Department of Psychology conducting psychological and psychiatric research on psychotherapy and trauma.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral researcher in environmental microbial ecology
jobs.description:
The Department of Biology, Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a two-year, fixed-term postdoctoral position in environmental microbial ecology, starting 1 February, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is part of a project funded by the Villum Foundation's Villum Experiment programme.

The project
Electrically conductive iron minerals are widespread in anoxic aquatic sediments, yet we know little about the microorganisms that live on them. The project aims to characterize the phylogenetic identity and ecophysiology of microorganisms associated with these minerals. We hypothesize that, by facilitating extracellular electron transfer, the minerals provide a distinct niche that selectively enriches electroactive microorganisms relative to the surrounding sediment.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two–year position from 1 February, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 
This is a fixed-term position to end on 31 January, 2029.

Job description
You will identify, visualize and characterize bacterial and archaeal cells associated with iron minerals by combining fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and correlative imaging, DNA- and/or RNA-based omics, and stable isotope incubation experiments. You will have considerable freedom to shape the methodological approach and to develop your own ideas within the project framework. Project collaborators in Germany will contribute chemical characterization of the minerals, giving you the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary team. Participation in supervision of BSc., MSc. and PhD students and possibly some classroom teaching is also expected.

Your profile
You hold a PhD in biology, earth and environmental science, biotechnology or a related field (or expect to complete it before the start date), and you have a research background in microbiology or microbial ecology.

Essentials:

• Experience with advanced microscopy and/or molecular microbial ecology methods.
• Interest in microbial physiology and electromicrobiology.
• A systematic approach to method development and testing.
• A publication record in international peer-reviewed journals, relative to your career stage.
• Very good written and oral communication skills in English.
Desirable:

• Experience with FISH, correlative microscopy, stable isotope probing, or omics data analysis.
• Experience working with sediment or other environmental samples.
• Experience with microbial physiology and/or electromicrobiology.
• If you are excited about the project but your experience does not match every point, we still encourage you to apply.
At the Department of Biology, we value a collegial and inclusive working environment and place strong emphasis on good relationships among colleagues and students. We welcome colleagues who bring an open, constructive and collaborative approach.

Who we are
The Department of Biology (Aarhus University) provides a framework for research and teaching in all major biological subdisciplines. The department currently encompasses approximately 200 academic and technical staff and 45 PhD students while 400 students follow the BSc and MSc programs offered by the department. The Section for Microbiology (https://bio.au.dk/en/about-biology/sections/microbiology) employs 12 associate and full professors and offers a vibrant, international research environment for studying microbial physiology, evolution, ecology, and biogeochemistry. The section integrates basic and applied research, addressing the functions, eco-physiology, and evolution of microorganisms in natural and biotechnological systems. The section has well-equipped laboratories, a permanent support staff of highly skilled laboratory technicians, and access to advanced imaging facilities on the AU campus.

What we offer
• A two-year position in a stimulating, international research environment
• Access to state-of-the-art laboratories and imaging facilities.
• A work environment encouraging lively, open and critical discussion.
• A work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities.
• A workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is Aarhus University, and the place of employment is Section for Microbiology within the Department of Biology (https://bio.au.dk/en/), Aarhus University, Ny Munkegade 114, DK-8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

Contact information
Applicants seeking further information are invited to contact Assoc. Prof. Kasper Urup Kjeldsen at AU (kasperuk@bio.au.dk).

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 29 November, 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

jobs.occupation: Consultancy in Otorhinolaryngology, head and neck surgery combined with a clinical professorship in Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology

A clinical position as consultant of Otorhinolaryngology at the Department of ORL, Head and neck surgery and audiology at Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet is open for appointment from as soon as possible.

The position is combined with a 5-year externally funded position as clinical professor in Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

It is a requirement that the applicant is accepted for appointment of both the professorship and the consultancy.

The advertisement for the professorship is available from the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

About the department

The Department of Otorhinolaryngology and Audiology is responsible for the full spectrum of diagnostics and treatment within the ENT and audiological fields, encompassing both general patient care and highly specialized services. A total of more than 100 clinically active physicians is employed within the department. In addition, there is a high level of research activity, including among the clinical staff. The department currently has five formally affiliated professors, three of whom are clinical professors in otorhinolaryngology. As a university hospital department, it also has teaching obligations at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels, including for healthcare professionals beyond the medical field of both the primary and secondary health sector.

Clinical functions and focus areas of the department

The consultant position in head and neck surgery requires a strong interest and proven surgical expertise within malignant head and neck surgery. The ideal candidate will demonstrate solid experience in teaching and research, including involvement in undergraduate and postgraduate education, as well as supervision of PhD students. Emphasis is placed on candidates with a robust, long-standing, and continuous research background. The candidate is expected to have extensive knowledge and research experience with head and neck cancer epidemiology and documented experience with national registries and particularly with HPV-driven head and neck cancer. A broad knowledge of benign ENT conditions is also expected. Further the candidate should be active and involved in thyroid cancer research.

The position offers significant opportunities for further specialization and skill development within advanced surgical techniques, including the potential for training in robotic surgery. The consultant will also be expected to take on administrative responsibilities such as patient triage and task coordination.

As the department provides highly specialized ENT services at a university level, applicants must have documented surgical experience and a demonstrated research interest.

Applicants must submit documentation of board certification in Otorhinolaryngology. According to the regulations of the Capital Region of Denmark, applicants must have held a specialist certification for at least five years to be appointed as a consultant at Rigshospitalet, unless an exemption is granted. Furthermore, applicants must provide evidence of clinical experience within head and neck surgery, as well as documentation of scientific and educational activities.

Strong collaboration skills are essential, including the ability to work professionally and constructively in interdisciplinary teams.

Organizationally, the consultant will report to the Head of Department. For professional matters related specifically to head and neck surgery, reference will be made to the lead consultant in that subspecialty.

We offer a dynamic and rewarding position in a busy and active department housed in brand-new, state-of-the-art facilities. The position includes excellent opportunities for involvement in research and clinical development.

Work Schedule: The position includes on-call duty (approximately every 14 days), shared equally among the department’s consultants.

Salary and terms of employment will follow the applicable collective agreement.

Please note: The position is subject to regulations requiring a child protection certificate ("børneattest"). Employment is contingent upon the ability to present a clean certificate.

Research and teaching

With the establishment of the new position as Consultant in Otorhinolaryngology and Clinical Professor in Oto-rhino-laryngology with special focus on Head & Neck Surgery, the Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery and Audiology seek to significantly strengthen leadership and strategic development within clinical research and teaching. The professorship is conceived as a pivotal academic and clinical role that will unify and advance research activities across the specialty, with a particular emphasis on translational and interdisciplinary head and neck research.

The position will serve as an academic anchor not only for Rigshospitalet but also for Nordsjællands Hospital and, more broadly, for Region Østdanmark (RØST), with the explicit ambition of fostering coordinated research efforts across Eastern Denmark. The clinical professor is expected to provide academic leadership, facilitate collaboration between hospital departments and regional research environments, and contribute to the development of shared research strategies and priorities across institutions.

In research, the position entails responsibility for initiating, leading, and consolidating high-quality clinical and translational research programmes within head and neck surgery and related disciplines. This includes strengthening existing research groups, promoting multicentre and cross-regional studies, supporting early-career researchers, and ensuring integration of research activities across hospitals within RØST. The professor will play a key role in attracting external funding, enhancing national and international visibility, and embedding research as a core component of clinical practice throughout Eastern Denmark.

In teaching, the position carries responsibility for academic leadership in undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing medical education within otorhinolaryngology and head and neck surgery. The professor will contribute to curriculum development, pedagogical innovation, and supervision at all levels, ensuring alignment between clinical training, academic standards, and regional workforce needs. Teaching activities will be coordinated across clinical sites, thereby supporting a unified and high-quality educational environment for medical students, residents, and fellows within RØST.

Overall, the position is designed to function as a unifying professorship that integrates research, teaching, and clinical excellence across Nordsjællands Hospital, the wider hospital network in RØST, and academic partners, thereby strengthening the academic foundation and future development of the specialty across Eastern Denmark.

Qualifications

Applicants must be board-certified specialist in Oto-rhino-laryngology.

Conditions

In order to be considered, the applicant must send an application to both the Faculty (the professorship) and to the hospital (the consultancy) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the professorship. Appointment is conditioned by the fact that the applicant obtains both positions. This also applies to the applicants who are already employed as consultants at Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet.

Salary and Employment Conditions

The position is subject to the Collective Agreement for Specialist Doctors and Consultant Physicians (Overlæger) and the applicable Working Time Agreement between the Danish Regions and the relevant medical professional organization.

Detailed information on employment conditions, collective agreements, and salary levels can be found here:

• Collective Agreement: https://laeger.dk/foreninger/overlaegeforeningen/ok26-overlaegeforeningen

• Collective Agreement (PDF): https://laeger.dk/media/15odzzl1/overenskomst-for-speciallaeger-og-overlaeger-2026.pdf

• Salary information: https://www.regionh.dk/om-region-hovedstaden/fakta/arbejdsplads/sider/startloen.aspx

As clinical professor at least 50 % of the working time will be allocated to academic tasks (e.g., research, teaching, evaluation tasks and communication with the public) in agreement with the Head of Department of Department of Clinical Medicine at the University of Copenhagen. The remaining time will be allocated for clinical work in agreement with the head of Department of ORL, Head and neck surgery and audiology, Rigshospitalet. Additional support and details on the working conditions must be negotiated with the head of the Department of ORL, Head and neck sugery and audiology,Rigshospitalet.

Application procedure

The application must include the following:

• 
Curriculum Vitae and a complete list of publications

Copy of the authorization certificate for specialist in Otorhinolaryngology.

• 
A description of how the applicant is qualified as

• 
Clinical expert

Communicator

• 
Collaborator

• 
Manager/administrator/organizer

• 
Health advocate

• 
Scholar/researcher/teacher

• 
Professional

For more information, please refer to Sundhedsstyrelsen: The Seven Roles of Physicians.

The closing date for applications is 8. November 2026.

Further information
